faq: What format should my product data be in?
A spreadsheet is best, but a supplier link, a PDF or a folder of photos with notes also works. We tell you in advance if anything is missing, such as prices or sizes, so nothing is guessed.
Can you upload products from a supplier or another store?
Yes, from supplier feeds, spreadsheets or your own other store, as long as you have the right to use the images and text. We do not copy other sellers' listings or protected brand content.
Will you publish the products straight away?
We can add them as drafts first and send you a review list, or publish them live if you prefer. Either way, we check each page on the storefront before we call it done.
What if I have more products than my package covers?
We upload the number in your package first, then quote the rest at a fair per-product rate. You can also add the extra 50 product add-on to the order now.
desc:
Shopify product uploads and editing means getting your catalog into the store accurately, with the right images, variants, prices and descriptions. Ecom Swift LLC loads or updates your products in your own account and checks each one on the live storefront.

## What are Shopify product uploads?

Shopify product uploads are the work of entering products into your store: titles, descriptions, variants, prices, SKUs, images, tags and collections. The same service covers editing products that already exist, whether that is one fix or a bulk change across the catalog.

You can send a spreadsheet, a supplier link or a folder of photos. We turn that raw material into finished product pages that a shopper can read and buy from.

## Why careful product data matters

A product page is where the buying decision happens. If the title is vague, the photos are dark or the variants are mislabeled, shoppers cannot tell what they are getting. They leave, or they buy the wrong size and return it.

Errors also spread. One wrong price in a spreadsheet becomes a wrong price on the site and in every feed that reads from it. Duplicate products split reviews and sales. Missing alt text means the images are invisible to screen readers and carry less meaning for search engines.

## How accurate listings help sales and search

Clear titles and honest descriptions answer the questions shoppers have before they ask them. Consistent variants let people pick size and color without confusion. Sharp images in the same style make the store look organized and trustworthy.

Structure helps both people and search engines. Tags and collections let shoppers browse by type, season or price, and they let you build sale pages quickly. Titles, descriptions and alt text give Google clear signals about what each page is about. Sales depend on your products, pricing and traffic, but clean data means the page is never the reason a shopper gives up.

## What a good product upload includes

- A title that names the product the way shoppers search for it.
- A description that is short, clear and written in your own words.
- Variants and options, such as size and color, set up with correct prices.
- SKUs entered so stock and orders are easy to match.
- Images uploaded in a consistent size, with descriptive alt text.
- Tags and collection assignments that follow one naming system.
- Metafields filled where your theme uses them, for details such as material or care.
- A draft review step before anything goes live.
- A storefront check of each product on phone and desktop.
- Cleanup of duplicates and broken product records.

## What we do

We begin by reading your source files and noting any gaps, such as a missing price or an image without a match. We send you those questions together, so you can answer in one go. Then we load the products as drafts in your Shopify admin.

Each product gets its title, description, variants, price, SKU, images and tags. On the Standard package we organize collections and options and send you the drafts to review before publishing. Premium adds rewritten descriptions for clarity, metafields where you use them and cleanup of duplicate or broken products. When the work is done, you receive a short checklist of what was added and anything we could not finish without your input.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Send data in one tidy sheet with one product per row, or one variant per row.
- Name image files after the product, so we can match them correctly.
- Keep one style for titles, such as brand, product and key feature.
- Tell us which products to publish now and which to keep as drafts.
- Check the drafts and reply with changes before they go live.

**Avoid:**
- Copying supplier descriptions word for word, which hurts search visibility.
- Mixing currencies or units in the same price column.
- Uploading very large image files that slow the page.
- Using ten near-identical collections for the same group of products.
- Publishing products before the images and prices are checked.

## Who this is for

This service suits new sellers who have a supplier list but no time to type it in. It suits shops moving from another platform, which need their catalog rebuilt cleanly, and it suits busy owners who are adding a new range every season. It also suits stores whose catalog became messy over time and needs a clean-up.

## What we need from you

Send your product data, photos and any supplier link, along with a collaborator or staff invitation to your store. If you have more products than your package covers, we can add more or divide the work in stages. We never need your password. We will ask you only for what we cannot decide ourselves, such as prices that are missing from the source. Everything is created inside your account, so you own it from the start.
